newsitem.title: USA: UAW sets strike deadline at GM Cadillac plant.
newsitem.headline: UAW sets strike deadline at GM Cadillac plant.

text.p: The United Auto Workers union said Friday it set a strike deadline against General Motors Corp.'s Cadillac assembly plant in Detroit for just before midnight on Aug. 8.

UAW spokesman Reg McGhee said the issues between GM and UAW Local 22 at the plant were the same staffing and health and safety issues that have plagued contract talks all year. Farming out work to outside suppliers was also a point of contention in the talks, he said.
GM settled a three-day strike July 25 at an engine and transmission plant in Warren, Mich., that had forced GM to shut down six car assembly plants and idle 16,500 workers.
The world's largest automaker has been hit by six strikes and faced several strike deadlines since January as it worked to reach local contract agreements.

GM and the UAW signed a national labour contract in November but the company has run into resistance from union locals as it seeks to shrink its work force through attrition and send more work to outside suppliers.
The Detroit-Hamtramck facility produces the Cadillac Seville, Eldorado and Deville. GM said it has 3,500 hourly workers at the plant.
